## Solution

We claim:

$$\lim_{|h|\to\infty} \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} |f(y+h)+f(y)|^p\,dy \;=\; 2\,\|f\|_p^p \;=\; 2\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|f(y)|^p\,dy.$$

---

### Step 1. The key elementary inequality

For $0<p<\infty$ there is a constant $C_p$ with
$$|a+b|^p \le C_p\bigl(|a|^p+|b|^p\bigr), \qquad C_p=\max(1,\,2^{p-1}).$$
(For $0<p\le 1$ this is subadditivity $|a+b|^p\le|a|^p+|b|^p$; for $p\ge1$ it follows from convexity of $t\mapsto t^p$.)

Consequently, for every $f\in L^p$ and every $h$,
$$\int|f(y+h)+f(y)|^p\,dy \le C_p\int\bigl(|f(y+h)|^p+|f(y)|^p\bigr)\,dy = 2C_p\,\|f\|_p^p. \tag{1}$$

---

### Step 2. Verification for $g\in C_c(\mathbb{R}^n)$

Let $g$ be continuous with compact support $K$. When $|h|>\operatorname{diam}(K)$, the sets $K$ and $K-h=\{y:y+h\in K\}$ are disjoint. Hence for each $y$ at most one of $g(y+h)$, $g(y)$ is nonzero, so
$$|g(y+h)+g(y)|^p = |g(y+h)|^p + |g(y)|^p \quad\text{(pointwise)}.$$
Integrating and using translation-invariance of Lebesgue measure,
$$\int|g(y+h)+g(y)|^p\,dy = \int|g(y+h)|^p\,dy+\int|g(y)|^p\,dy = 2\|g\|_p^p. \tag{2}$$

---

### Step 3. Stability of the functional under $L^p$-perturbation

Set $\Phi_h(f):=\int|f(y+h)+f(y)|^p\,dy$. We show $|\Phi_h(f)-\Phi_h(g)|$ is controlled by $\|f-g\|_p$ **uniformly in $h$**, in two regimes.

**Case $0<p\le 1$.** Subadditivity gives $||a|^p-|b|^p|\le|a-b|^p$, so
$$|\Phi_h(f)-\Phi_h(g)|\le\int|(f-g)(y+h)+(f-g)(y)|^p\,dy\le\int\bigl(|f-g|(y+h))^p+|f-g|(y)|^p\bigr)\,dy=2\|f-g\|_p^p. \tag{3}$$

**Case $p\ge 1$.** By the mean-value inequality $||a|^p-|b|^p|\le p(|a|^{p-1}+|b|^{p-1})|a-b|$, with $a=f(y+h)+f(y)$, $b=g(y+h)+g(y)$, and Hölder with exponents $p/(p-1)$ and $p$:
$$|\Phi_h(f)-\Phi_h(g)|\le 2p\bigl(\Phi_h(f)^{(p-1)/p}+\Phi_h(g)^{(p-1)/p}\bigr)\|f-g\|_p.$$
Using the uniform bound (1), $\Phi_h(f)^{(p-1)/p}\le(2C_p)^{(p-1)/p}\|f\|_p^{p-1}$, and similarly for $g$, so
$$|\Phi_h(f)-\Phi_h(g)|\le M(p,f,g)\,\|f-g\|_p \tag{4}$$
with $M$ independent of $h$.

In both regimes, also $|\,2\|f\|_p^p-2\|g\|_p^p\,|\le K(p,f,g)\|f-g\|_p^{\min(p,1)}$ by the same inequalities applied to $|f|^p,|g|^p$.

---

### Step 4. Density argument

Let $\varepsilon>0$. Since $C_c(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is dense in $L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for $0<p<\infty$, pick $g\in C_c$ with $\|f-g\|_p$ so small that the bounds (3)/(4) and the analogous bound on $|2\|f\|_p^p-2\|g\|_p^p|$ are each $<\varepsilon/3$.

Then for every $h$,
$$\bigl|\Phi_h(f)-2\|f\|_p^p\bigr|\le\underbrace{|\Phi_h(f)-\Phi_h(g)|}_{<\varepsilon/3}+\underbrace{|\Phi_h(g)-2\|g\|_p^p|}_{=0\text{ for }|h|\text{ large, by (2)}}+\underbrace{|2\|g\|_p^p-2\|f\|_p^p|}_{<\varepsilon/3}<\varepsilon$$
for all $|h|$ sufficiently large. Since $\varepsilon>0$ was arbitrary,

$$\boxed{\lim_{|h|\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|f(y+h)+f(y)|^p\,dy = 2\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|f(y)|^p\,dy.}$$
